Subset of recorded decisions, not policy replay or opportunity recall.

semantics: PREPARE_HOST ACK is a Host shadow backup, not an HBM offload. Demotion records are per native node/pool release; repeated events and shared prefixes are not whole-agent offloads or unique bytes. Tool matching uses workflow/invocation plus the latest submitted context/epoch and exact tool_run_id. A decision requires exactly one tool active on the harness monotonic clock. When all tools in the same bounded context/epoch already ended, the latest end is retained as a nonpositive remaining-time label and a false long-wait decision, rather than dropping it from precision. Unclosed or ambiguous boundaries stay unknown. Event wall time is converted using the latest preceding paired scheduler census or runtime-state sample, so millisecond clock pairing uncertainty remains. Only preceding accepted forecasts enter reconstructed predictions; subsequent tool ends are labels only. The 2000ms precision measures whether selected waits remain open long enough, not RETURN timestamp accuracy, recall, benefit or performance. It remains a fixed reference alongside the per-record offload horizon stored in accepted forecasts; legacy logs without that field use 2000ms. Independent-tool precision uses its first observed action in that category; per-node decision counts do not constitute independent samples. Long-tool total duration is only descriptive; it is not an opportunity denominator because pressure, residency, references, Host capacity and forecasting coverage are not continuously observed. Native untagged eviction and terminal child discard are separate. No unconditional post-spawn COMMIT_CPU is inferred from these events.
